clue.text: Woman can be seen as liable to divorce

parts.note: Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana
something that can be seen is visible

explanation.surface: A woman is in plain view, apparently a candidate for divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce is to separate, so something able to be split apart is liable to be divorced in the old sense.

clue.text: Wide mouth displayed by model talking

indicators.note: displayed by says the letters are on show inside the words model talking

explanation.surface: A model is chatting with her mouth wide open.
explanation.definitionFit: A river's fan-shaped outlet into the sea is a broad estuary.

clue.text: Half the team holding an orchid

indicators.note: holding says one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: Villa is half the name of Aston Villa, an English football club

explanation.surface: Half a sports side is clutching a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football team; Villa is one of its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The flavouring pod comes from a climbing orchid.

clue.text: One taking the time to find the best in the sample

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a swatch is a sample of fabric
to top is to beat or be the best

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time picking the best item from a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer used at races measures how long something takes.

clue.text: Struggle to put on uniform

parts.note: a battle is a struggle
to dress is to put clothes on

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to get into a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat clothing is the soldier's standard field outfit.

clue.text: I must leave Hebridean island where I originated

indicators.note: must leave says a letter is to be taken out

parts.note: Eigg is one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone must quit the Scottish island of their birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'I' is a person; the definition's 'I' is a chick, which came from an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Every bird hatches from a shell laid by its mother.

clue.text: Senior officer in charge gives one the gripes

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A senior officer in command upsets the stomach of one of his men.
explanation.definitionFit: The gripes is an old name for sharp abdominal pains, the trouble a baby with wind suffers.

clue.text: All one's work found in a chapter

explanation.surface: An author's complete output is located within one chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's accepted body of works is so called, and a cathedral chapter includes clergy with this title.

clue.text: Falsely claimed to have the rest

parts.note: to have lied is to have falsely claimed
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone falsely said they owned the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nap on the bed is a brief break or repose.

clue.text: The cads one's thrashed and beaten

indicators.note: thrashed signals the letters are beaten about into a new order

parts.note: one's is one is, I plus S

explanation.surface: The bounders are thrashed and beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punished physically, flogged, is to be chastised.

clue.text: Infantry excluded from set-piece in contest

parts.note: line regiments are the regular infantry of an army
someone excluded is left out

explanation.surface: Foot soldiers are left out of a planned move in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, a line-out is the set restart when the ball has gone into touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby restart from touch is a rehearsed set move within a match.

clue.text: Private article found in bed

parts.note: a gunner is a private soldier in the artillery
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A soldier and a newspaper piece turn up under the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a sleeping one: gunnera is a giant-leaved garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunnera is a huge rhubarb-like plant grown in garden borders.

clue.text: A light-hearted cartoonist with a feeling of satisfaction

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only the middle of light is used

parts.note: David Low was a famous British political cartoonist

explanation.surface: A cheerful cartoonist feels pleased with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone glowing with pleasure is radiant with contentment.

clue.text: Spending money on funeral preparations

explanation.surface: Someone is paying out for the arrangements after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying out cash is spending it, and laying out a corpse is preparing it for burial.

clue.text: Warning not to wait for part in Coward's play?

parts.note: a coward is called yellow
an actor's part in a play consists of lines

explanation.surface: A warning not to hang around, given to an actor in a Noel Coward play.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was a playwright, but here a coward is yellow. Double yellow lines on a British road forbid parking.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted kerbside stripes in Britain forbid stopping or parking.

clue.text: For example, Red Marshal took it in prison once

definitions.text: For example, Red Marshal took it in prison once

parts.words: For example, Red Marshal took it in prison once
parts.note: the word follows Red to name a body of water, and follows Marshal to name an old London debtors' prison

explanation.surface: A communist marshal was once locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was a notorious debtors' prison in Southwark, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is an example of an ocean arm, and the Marshalsea was a jail.

clue.text: Husband in difficulty over a little money — what's here is no use

indicators.note: in says the husband goes inside the difficulty

parts.note: a scrape is a tricky situation
p is a penny, a small sum of British money

explanation.surface: A husband in money trouble finds his worthless belongings piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dump for discarded items holds things of no further value.

clue.text: Pastime provides a merry few moments

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, merry
forty winks or a few winks is a short nap, a few moments

explanation.surface: A hobby gives a tipsy short sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicking-counters game is a children's amusement or recreation.

clue.text: Failed as diver?

parts.note: a phrase for failing or going bust also describes what a diver does by sinking below the surface

explanation.definitionFit: Going bust is collapsing, and a diver literally submerges.

clue.text: Request for help in alighting not made specially

explanation.surface: A passenger asks for a hand getting off, in clothes bought off the rack.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks someone to lift you down, and as a noun means ready-made or second-hand clothing.

clue.text: Colleague admits love of haughtily appearing

indicators.note: admits says the colleague lets the next pieces inside

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or partner
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A colleague confesses to a love of looking superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with cold reserve, distant and superior, is acting disdainfully.

clue.text: It's a little cleaner in the South of France

explanation.surface: Something is slightly more hygienic down in Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: One bubble of soapy lather is a small piece of detergent, and the French word for south is spelt this way.

clue.text: Cook would change top of this vegetable

indicators.note: says the first letter of this answer is swapped to give the word for cook

parts.note: to cook the books is to falsify them

explanation.surface: A chef wants to alter the top of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: change the first letter S of the answer to F and it gives FALSIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsify is a root crop, sometimes called oyster plant.

clue.text: Governor to take advice mostly from professional

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used except for its final letter

parts.note: to consult is to seek advice

explanation.surface: A governor seeks counsel, chiefly from an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' removes the last letter T from CONSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman provincial ruler was the official in charge of a province.

clue.text: Old actor rejected by a Normandy theatre

indicators.note: rejected says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a ham is a poor overacting actor

explanation.surface: An elderly performer is turned down by a French playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns HAM into MAH. The theatre is a theatre of war: one of the D-Day landing beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the 1944 D-Day landing beaches was a zone of military operations.

clue.text: In the dark, until letters are exchanged

indicators.note: swapping letters around in until rearranges the word into a new one

explanation.surface: Someone stays unaware until a letter swap happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the T and L of UNTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere without lights switched on is dark, without illumination.

clue.text: Lily perhaps is such a forceful personality

explanation.surface: A woman called Lily has a dominant character.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger lily is a flower, and a ferocious big cat stands for a fierce, aggressive person.

clue.text: Fell out with small people's country

indicators.note: out signals the word fell is knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone fell out with the small nation's people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland is the realm of tiny magical folk.

clue.text: Cheated in two ways

indicators.note: in two ways says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone was swindled twice over, by two different methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who swindled you conned or diddled you.

clue.text: Agreeing to be casual sort of acquaintance

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to be merely a passing acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowing the head shows assent, and a slight familiarity is a nodding acquaintance.

clue.text: One said to be recording taxonomic divisions

indicators.note: said to be signals the word sounds like another spoken out loud

parts.note: a filer is one who records documents by filing them

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently recording biological classifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists group animals into large ranks below kingdom, each one a phylum.

clue.text: One who dispatches a warship

explanation.surface: Someone sends off a naval vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer finishes off victims, and a fast naval escort vessel bears this name.
